subject: Feature matrix + integration options — post-demo summary
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Feature matrix + integration options — post-demo summary

Hi Liam — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side with the items we agreed to validate and the tradeoffs we discussed. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Top pain & goal (per call)
- Novida needs sub-200ms median latency for triage suggestions at 512 tokens, predictable tail latency for peak hours.
- Must keep PHI off our hosted model; preference for VPC/private deployment but open to Dedicated if it simplifies rollout.

Integration options we covered (pros/cons)
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, but you'd have to accept encrypted PHI-in-transit and our standard SOC2 boundary. Good for non-PHI features (summaries, metadata).
- Dedicated: predictable throughput with reserved GPUs; supports stricter logging controls and per-tenant isolation. Slightly higher commit.
- Private (VPC): aligns best with compliance — customer-managed VPC & KMS; longer lead time for infra onboarding.

Product fit notes (actionable items)
1) Streaming vs batch — for low latency we recommend streaming generation with prefix KV caching; tradeoff is slightly more memory on serving nodes. We'll prototype a streaming path in Dedicated to validate tail behavior.
2) Function calling / structured outputs — we can push strict JSON schema enforcement in the runtime with schema validation hooks; Monica will sketch a sample schema for your triage event output.
3) Embeddings + reranking — we suggested server-side dense embed store + lightweight cross-encoder rerank for top-5 precision; metric target: top-1 accuracy uplift >= 12% vs current heuristic.

Next steps (agreed)
- Redwood: share an integration feature matrix and an initial MLP for Dedicated vs Private (attachment). (Action: Sergio) — by EOD 5/19
- Novida: provide sample anonymized trace (latency histogram + token distributions) and security contacts. (Action: Liam) — by 5/22
- Joint: 2-hour technical deep-dive with infra + SRE to scope VPC onboarding and certs. Tentative week of 5/25. (Action: Sergio + Monica)

Attachments: redwood-integration-feature-matrix.xlsx (includes cost/latency estimates, quantization profiles, and SDK change impact).

Thanks — attaching a short bullets doc so your engineering team can quickly scan.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez

Thanks for the clear recap, Sergio — that captures the call well. A couple clarifications from our side:

- PHI scope: for the triage feature we will need all clinical notes redacted before anything leaves our network. That makes Private or Dedicated with specific KMS controls a hard requirement.
- Latency: 200ms median is aspirational; 99th percentile constraints matter more for UX. We'll share traces tomorrow.
- Reranking: we like the hybrid embed + cross-encoder idea. Can you include an estimate of the cost delta for running a cross-encoder in Dedicated vs offloading rerank to our CPU layer?

Also looping in procurement — can Redwood share a sample Reserved Capacity commitment term sheet or examples?

Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Product, Novida Health

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Feature matrix + integration options — post-demo summary

Hi Liam — quick technical notes from our side to narrow scope before the deep-dive: 

- Function calling / structured output: we'll prototype a strict schema enforcement plugin that rejects malformed outputs and emits parseability metrics to your audit log. Expect a proof-of-concept within the deep-dive.
- Streaming memory: for 512-token median with KV caching, estimate +20% memory headroom on GPU. If you prefer lower memory, we can evaluate 4-bit quantization profiles; tradeoff is slightly noisier generations on rare clinical terms.
- Rerank placement: cross-encoder on GPU Dedicated will give best precision but increases per-request cost ~2.8x vs CPU-based approximate rerank. We'll put exact numbers in the feature matrix.

I'll prepare a short sample schema for the triage event (fields, types, enums) and attach it to the MLP.

--
